title: Moving around
summary: Open anything without leaving your place, go back, search everything, and keep a case in view.

sections.heading: The inspector
paragraphs: Underlined names are links to a finding, document, agency, entity, request or case. Hover one to preview it; click it to open it in the inspector on the right. The view underneath stays where it was.
A link inside the inspector opens another layer on top. The trail at the top walks back through the layers, and Esc steps back one layer at a time.

A finding opens as its evidence chain: the claim, what it was measured on, each cited passage, the file that holds it, and that file's last provenance check. A link the record does not have is shown as missing.

sections.heading: Back and forward
paragraphs: The back button at the top left names the view it returns to. Cmd-[ and Cmd-], the mouse back and forward buttons, and Go back in the command palette step through the views you visited, with their filters, selection and scroll position.

sections.heading: Search everything
paragraphs: Cmd-K searches findings, agencies, entities, request records and document passages as well as commands. Choosing a result opens it in the inspector. A sentence is treated as a question and answered from findings, the entity graph and document text; no AI model is used.

sections.heading: How far back "new" reaches
paragraphs: The clock control on the San Diego and Story desk views sets the window: since you last opened the app, the last 24 hours, 7 days, 30 days, or any time. It filters on when something was first found. It does not show what the records looked like on an earlier date.

sections.heading: The case you are working
paragraphs: The case button in the toolbar keeps one case in view. Choose a case to work it; open it to see its requests and cited sources in the inspector, or open its casework. A remembered case that no longer exists is shown as not found rather than silently cleared.

While a case is active, the San Diego and Story desk views show only findings that cite or concern the case's source documents or the requests that hold them, and the Evidence view lists those requests. A bar says so; Show everything turns it off. If the case's scope does not load, nothing is hidden and the bar says why.

sections.heading: Undo a dismissal
paragraphs: Dismissing a finding shows Undo for ten seconds. Undo returns the finding to the list with its original discovery date. A restored finding is removed on the next sweep like any other if its detector no longer reports it.
